text:
sophie (Comms): Quick follow-up from the postmortem — we need to finalize customer-facing summary language and the exact RCA sharing flow. Who can own the redaction checklist?

raj (SRE): I can take the redaction checklist draft. Will need legal sign-off for any PII guidance.

maria (Customer Success): +1. Also want to confirm timing: customers get a short summary within 72 hours, full RCA after validation and redaction?

oliver (Legal): Confirming — 72h is fine for a short incident summary. For RCAs, legal needs visibility before external distribution if any customer data is involved. Will review redaction checklist.

jake (PM): Heads-up: product wants standard statuspage copy we can reuse across incidents. Can we agree on a lightweight template?

sophie (Comms): Draft template below. Please comment inline.

```
Status page blurb (short): "We experienced elevated error rates impacting <service>. Our engineers mitigated the issue by <mitigation>. Users may have seen failed requests between <start> and <end>. A full investigation is underway; a follow-up summary will be published within 72 hours."

Full customer summary (72h): bullet list of impact, mitigation, next steps, who to contact.

RCA (post-redaction): detailed timeline, root cause, remediation & owner, expected completion date, link to postmortem.
```

raj (SRE): Looks good. For the RCA redaction checklist I propose these items: 
- remove PII/keys/credentials
- redact internal hostnames tied to customers
- summarize, not quote, customer logs

maria (Customer Success): Can we add a consent step if we want to include a customer quote or a specific example that references them?

oliver (Legal): Yes. Include a consent flag. If a customer is identifiable or quoted we need explicit consent from the customer and approval from legal.

incident-bot: Reminder: create task in #incidents-actions with a 72h due date.

sophie (Comms): Assigning action items: 
- redaction checklist: raj (owner) — due in 48h
- statuspage template & shortcopy: sophie (owner) — due in 24h
- consent process doc: oliver (owner) — due in 72h
- customer comms playbook update (how & when to escalate): maria (owner) — due in 5 business days

jake (PM): One procedural ask: add a field to postmortem template for "recurring-pattern-check" so we can flag incidents that match previous ones. That helps decide if proactive comms are needed.

raj (SRE): Good call. I can wire a checklist item to query past 6 months for similar alerts and include a short note in the RCA.

maria (Customer Success): Also request: when we send initial 72h summary, include an explicit "what we're doing for you" section so CS teams can reuse text for customer outreach.

sophie (Comms): Agreed. We'll add a 3-line "for your customers" snippet to the 72h summary template.

oliver (Legal): For the redaction checklist doc, I'll add a short appendix with examples of unacceptable content and a simple sign-off flow: redaction -> legal review -> comms review -> publish.

raj (SRE): I'll open the PR for the checklist and link the sample queries to detect recurring patterns.

sophie (Comms): Thanks — action owners noted. I'll follow up with a short Slack thread per owner and create the tasks in the incidents tracker. Please react with :+1: when you accept the assignment.

raj (SRE): :+1:

maria (Customer Success): :+1:

oliver (Legal): :+1:

jake (PM): :+1:

sophie (Comms): Leaving this thread open for any edge cases (e.g., regulated customers, air-gapped deployments). If anything else pops up, tag me.

incident-bot: Task created: INCIDENT-4527 (customer-comms-followup) — due 2024-07-24

sophie (Comms): FYI, I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to walk through the checklist and sign-off flow. Invite to follow.
